title: Protocol for batch imaging and quantification of cellular mismatch during Drosophila embryonic heart formation
protocol: Harvest overnight embryo plate in the morning.
Add approximately 2 mL halocarbon oil into the plate.
Rotate the plate to ensure even coverage with oil.
Identify early stage 16 embryos using completed dorsal closure and three hindgut segments under a stereomicroscope.
Select approximately 50–100 embryos using a micro dissecting probe.
Transfer selected embryos to a marked region on the plate.
Prepare a small filter paper (∼1 cm²) and place it on the Petri dish lid.
Add one or two drops of fresh bleach solution onto the filter paper.
Transfer harvested embryos to the surface of the bleach-infiltrated filter paper.
Dechorionate embryos in bleach-infiltrated filter paper for ∼1–2 minutes until their chorion detaches.
Pick up the filter paper (with embryos attached) by tweezer and attach it to a paper towel to dry it.
Add three drops of water onto a plate, move the dried filter paper with embryos to one drop of water and wash it for 10 seconds; repeat this process three times in total.
Use a micro dissecting probe under a stereomicroscope to pick up dechorionated and washed embryos and transfer them into a 5-mL glass vial containing ∼1 mL of formaldehyde-saturated heptane.
Incubate the embryos in the solution on a nutator for 1 hour at room temperature.
Transfer the embryos from the vial to a small petri dish lid using a glass pipette, ensuring they stay in the neck of the pipette during transfer.
Allow the heptane to evaporate (∼30 seconds) and immediately cover the embryos with PBS solution (∼2 mL).
Use a stereomicroscope to monitor the procedure.
Mount a 23-gauge needle on a 3-mL syringe.
Poke a small hole at the surface of the vitelline membrane at the anterior end of the embryo with the needle.
Gently push the fixed embryos out from the vitelline membrane through the hole by applying pressure.
Add 100 μL Triton X-100 into the PBS solution in the petri dish lid.
Pipette solution to mix the solution and allow the embryos to float up.
Collect and transfer the devitellinized embryos to a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube using a 200 μL pipette.
Rinse the fixed embryos with 1% BSA/PBT.
Wash the fixed embryos twice with 1% BSA/PBT on a nutator for 20 minutes each time.
Block the embryos with 10% BSA/PBT for 1 hour on a nutator.
Remove the blocking medium and add primary antibodies diluted in 5% BSA/PBT.
Incubate the primary antibody on a nutator at 4°C overnight.
Wash the sample four times with 1% BSA/PBT.
Add secondary antibody diluted in 5% BSA/PBT for 2 hours at room temperature.
Wash the sample three times with PBT.
Mount embryos on a microscope slide using a coverslip taped to one end of the slide.
Transfer embryos (∼50–100) to the center of the coverslip.
Dry the samples using filter paper.
Add one drop of Aqua-mount medium on top of the embryos and spread gently.
Place the slide under a stereomicroscope.
Move the embryos next to each other in a line using a probe.
Orientate the embryos so that either dorsal side or ventral side is facing up.
Add another drop of Aqua-mount medium at the side of the embryos.
Gently angle a 22 × 22 sized coverslip over the sample with one edge touching the 22×50 coverslip.
Lower the top coverslip gently over the sample.
Seal the top coverslip with nail polish.
Keep the slide in darkness overnight to ensure the medium dries before imaging.
Apply post-fixation for 20 min with 4% formaldehyde/PBT after completing steps 1–8 for the first primary antibody.
Repeat from step 1 to step 8 for the second primary antibody in sequential staining procedure.
Store primary antibodies at 4°C for reuse after initial incubation.
Align embryos next to each other in Aqua-mount mounting medium.
Keep the process short, normally within half an hour.
Avoid using sticky mounting medium; add another drop if necessary.
